title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 206 (Notice of revocation or renunciation)

content.overview: Reasonable notice must be given of such revocation or renunciation; otherwise, the damage thereby resulting to the principal or the agent, as the case may be, must be made good to the one by the other.
content.glance: Reasonable notice of revocation or renunciation required; otherwise damages must be made good.
content.study: Reasonable notice must be given of such revocation or renunciation; otherwise, the damage thereby resulting to the principal or the agent, as the case may be, must be made good to the one by the other.

sections.heading: Reasonable notice
sections.body: Reasonable notice must be given of revocation or renunciation.

sections.heading: Damages if no notice
sections.body: Otherwise, damage resulting to the other party must be made good.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 206 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Test whether reasonable notice was given; if not, assess damage to the other party.
